panels.text: 1831. Michael Faraday is experimenting with electricity and magnetism.
The rule that bears his name, Faraday's law of induction, says a changing magnetic field can induce an electric current in a circuit.

The same year he builds the Faraday disc: a conducting disc turning in a magnetic field, which creates a potential difference. It is the first homopolar generator, very inefficient and not used as a practical source of power.
The twist: his principle runs the world. Steam, gas, water and wind turbines, even hand cranks, can spin generators, and generators produce nearly all the electric power on worldwide grids.
